question: Türkiye is annoyed about the legitimate choices the Greek Government has made to protect Greece. Ankara is bothered by Greece’s relations with Israel, France and the United States. It is deeply annoyed about being excluded from SAFE defence funding. The Turks have even gone as far as to threaten the energy giant Chevron, which operates south of Crete. Meanwhile, Türkiye is peddling the Blue Homeland narrative, which is directed against Greece’s sovereignty, with statements by top officials. In view of the above: 1.
Will the Commission continue to provide EU funds to Türkiye when the latter is threatening an EU country?
When does the Commission plan to apply financial safeguards to funds intended for non-EU countries when they persistently violate international law?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.8.2026) Türkiye is a candidate country and key partner for the EU. As reiterated by the Council of the European Union and the European Council1, the EU has a strategic interest in a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean, and in the development of a cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship with Türkiye.

The Commission engages with Türkiye in areas of joint interest, while also addressing concerns. The accession negotiations with Türkiye have been at a standstill since 2018, due to backsliding on the rule of law. As a result, the EU has reduced pre-accession support to Türkiye and has reoriented funding towards civil society, people-to-people contacts, and EU priorities.
In line with European Council conclusions of April 20242, the Commission is pursuing engagement with Türkiye in a phased, proportionate, and reversible manner.

The EU has underlined on numerous occasions that Türkiye must avoid threats and actions that damage good neighbourly relations and respect the sovereignty of all Member States over their territorial sea and airspace as well as all their sovereign rights, including the right to explore and exploit natural resources in accordance with EU and international law, in particular the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
The EU remains committed to defending its interests and those of its Member States as well as to upholding regional stability.
